newsitem.title: UK: BSM sees sharp drop in H1 profits.
newsitem.headline: BSM sees sharp drop in H1 profits.

text.p: Driving instruction company BSM Group Plc said on Monday its first-half pretax profits could be about half of last year's level, due to regulation changes for driving tests.
"BSM announces that it expects a significant reduction in profits before tax in the first half of 1997," the firm said in a statement.
BSM posted pre-tax profits of about 2.92 million stg for the first half of 1996 and a dividend of 2.53p.
BSM said it planned to cut its costs by 1.0 million stg on an annualised basis, mainly by closing 18 of its 154 branches.
The company also planned to keep its 1997 interim dividend at last year's level.
BSM shares fell more than 30 percent, dropping 43p to 98.5 by 1050 GMT.
BSM said driving test applications received by the Driving Standards Agency in the first quarter fell by 54 percent as a result of a regulation change.
The change meant that since January 1, learner drivers have been required to pass their theory tests before booking their practical driving tests.
